summary: A contractor who builds, repairs or improves real property is the consumer of its materials and pays tax on them; it does not charge sales tax to the owner in Idaho.

conditions.when: The contractor sells materials only, with no installation

citations.title: IDAPA 35.01.02 as published July 2017
citations.quote: Such contractors are defined as the consumers of the materials they install and are required to pay sales or use tax on their cost for the materials. They do not charge sales tax to their customers unless they make a sale of materials only, with no installation.

citations.title: IDAPA 35.01.02 (rules in force 2026-07-01)
citations.quote: A contractor is any person acting as a general contractor, subcontractor, contractee, subcontractee, or speculative builder who builds, alters, repairs, or improves real property.

citations.title: IDAPA 35.01.02 (rules in force 2026-07-01)
citations.quote: Contractors are the consumers of all the goods they use.

notes: Repair and improvement are treated alike, so one rule covers both subcodes. Idaho's only general local sales taxes are resort-city taxes; this ID rule covers the state 6% tax (and a local part where no ID:local rule exists). Where a code is taxed by the state, the ID:local rule for it says the resort-city tax depends on the city's ordinance. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from https://adminrules.idaho.gov/rules/current/35/350102.pdf to https://files.dfm.idaho.gov/dfm-admin-website/rules/current/35/350102.pdf. 2026-11-02: https://adminrules.idaho.gov/rules/current/35/0102.pdf is no longer online; its successor at https://files.dfm.idaho.gov/dfm-admin-website/rules/current/35/350102.pdf no longer carries the quoted sentence, so the citation keeps the archived copy.

summary: Whether an Idaho resort city's local sales tax applies to candy depends on that city's ordinance: some tax everything the state taxes, others only lodging, liquor by the drink and restaurant food.

conditions.when: The city's ordinance taxes all sales subject to the state sales tax, or names this kind of sale
The city limits its tax to other categories (e.g. lodging and alcohol by the drink only)

citations.title: Idaho State Tax Commission, City Sales Taxes
citations.quote: Resort cities have a choice in what’s taxed and can include everything that’s subject to the state sales tax.

citations.title: Idaho State Tax Commission, City Sales Taxes
citations.quote: Some, but not all, choose to limit the local sales tax to lodging, alcohol by the drink, and restaurant food.

citations.title: Idaho Code 50-1044
citations.quote: are hereby given the freedom to authorize their city government to adopt, implement and collect one (1) or more local-option nonproperty taxes as provided herein.

notes: 2013-07-01: the resort-city statute (Idaho Code 50-1044, added 1978) was last amended in 2013 (effective date assumed July 1, not checked); the Tax Commission page describing cities' choices was read 2026-10-30. Idaho's local sales taxes are resort-city option taxes (Idaho Code Title 50, ch. 10) whose base each city's ordinance sets; the ordinances were not read here, so the local part is left to the city. Cities without a local tax have no local part.
